the role of NMDA receptor in the tetanus-induced postsynaptic Ca(2+) increase in the young visual cortex.
the mechanisms of tetanus-induced increase of intracellular [Ca2+]i in the postsynaptic neurons.

the tetanic synaptic input to the postsynaptic neurons of the visual cortex of 2-week-old rats causes the increase in postsynapatic Ca2+ concentration via NMDA receptors, and this Ca2+ increase plays an important role in the induction of long-term potentiation in the visual cortex.

tetanic synaptic inputs induce a Ca2+ increase in the postsynaptic membrane in layer II/3 of the developing rat visual cortex, and that NMDA receptor activation is the major mechanism underlying the Ca2+-increase.
